assets.name: Dane_Tesla_1863
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 12 years old, lean build for his age, dark hair, serious expression. Taller than average for his age. Strong hands — the hands of a child who builds things, who draws constantly, who works with materials. His posture is the posture of someone who is thinking about something other than where he is standing.
assets.attire: Plain linen shirt, dark trousers, leather boots. Simple working clothes of a Serbian Orthodox priest's household in rural Croatia.
assets.notes: Nikola Tesla's older brother. Died in horse accident in Smiljan, 1863. No photographs exist. FLUX has no training data — full physique description required. The episode centers on his absence.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1863
assets.physique: Serbian boy, 7 years old, slight build, dark hair, wide-set eyes with an intensity that registers even in childhood. Tall for his age. Standing at the edge of a garden, completely still, watching something. His face holds the specific stillness of a child who has just seen something that will not leave.
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt and short dark trousers. Leather sandals. Rural Croatian peasant clothing of the 1860s.
assets.notes: Tesla as a child at the moment of witnessing Dane's accident. FLUX cannot render child Tesla from training data — needs description.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1891
assets.notes: Tesla at age 35. Working in his Grand Street laboratory. At the height of his powers — the polyphase motor patents, the transformer work, the early resonance experiments. Well-dressed, precise in his movements.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1943
assets.notes: Age 86. Final days in Hotel New Yorker Room 3327. Found dead January 7, 1943.

assets.name: Milutin_Tesla_1863
assets.physique: Serbian Orthodox priest, mid-40s, tall and lean with a full dark beard going grey at the edges. Deep-set eyes. High forehead. Scholarly bearing — the posture of a man who reads, who writes sermons, who keeps records. Hands roughened from outdoor life in a rural parish despite his clerical role.
assets.attire: Black Orthodox clerical robe with silver cross pendant. Black kamilavka cap. In informal scenes — plain dark coat over work clothes.
assets.notes: Tesla's father. Parish priest of Smiljan. Owned the horse that killed Dane. The horse had previously saved his life under undescribed circumstances.

assets.name: Djuka_Tesla_1865
assets.physique: Serbian woman, early 40s, strong build, dark hair pulled back tightly, hands roughened from farmwork and household manufacturing. Intense dark eyes. High cheekbones. An expression of concentrated grief wearing the mask of function — she is going through her son's belongings. She has not stopped moving since the accident because stopping would mean feeling what the task is actually about.
assets.attire: Simple dark linen dress, white apron. Head covered with a plain kerchief. Mourning dress for a rural Serbian Orthodox household.
assets.notes: Tesla's mother. Born Djuka Mandic. Writing a letter to her cousin in Gracac two years after Dane's death. Going through Dane's belongings. Found his notebook.

assets.name: MK_Elderly_Woman_1981
assets.physique: Croatian woman, 94 years old, small and sharp-featured, white hair pinned back, dark eyes that hold their focus despite her age. Weathered face with deep lines but alert expression. Sitting upright in her chair in a way that suggests she was raised to sit upright and has not stopped. Her hands rest on her lap, one over the other, the knuckles pronounced.
assets.attire: Dark housedress, black cardigan. Simple shoes. The clothing of a very old woman who still dresses carefully every morning.
assets.notes: Fictional elderly woman from Gospic identified only as M.K. in the Lika Cultural Documentation Society transcript. Her grandmother knew Djuka Tesla. Being interviewed about folk memories of the Tesla family. Becomes agitated when the interviewer corrects her grandmother's account.

assets.name: The_Dane_Figure_1891
assets.physique: Man in his late 30s or early 40s, tall, lean build similar to Nikola Tesla but with a different quality of stillness — where Tesla moves with precision and intent, this man moves with patience. Dark hair, clean-shaven. Standing at a blackboard covered in equations, back to the camera. His hand raised toward the board, writing. The handwriting is rounder and more deliberate than Tesla's angular script.
assets.attire: Dark wool trousers, white linen shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow. No jacket — working dress in a laboratory.
assets.notes: The alternate-timeline version of Dane Tesla as he appears in the laboratory photograph from the New Haven auction lot. Not shown face-forward. Depicted by his writing hand and posture only. The second man in the photograph — not identified by name in any caption.

assets.name: Smiljan_Garden_1863
assets.notes: The garden behind the Tesla family priest's house in Smiljan, Croatia, where Dane Tesla's accident occurred. Setting for the opening scene.

children.name: Garden_Courtyard_1863
children.physique: Small enclosed garden behind a stone farmhouse. Stone wall on three sides, fourth side open toward a barn. Packed dirt and short dry grass. A grey stallion stands near the barn opening, large for a working animal, weight shifting foot to foot. Summer heat — limestone dust in the air, wild thyme smell, bleached-white sky. The light is high and flat, the kind of summer light that removes all shadow from the midday ground.
children.notes: Where Dane Tesla died. Where Nikola Tesla, age 7, stood and witnessed the accident.

children.name: Tesla_Farmhouse_Smiljan_1863
children.physique: Stone farmhouse with whitewashed walls and a dark timber roof. Small windows with wooden shutters open to summer. A single oil lamp visible on a windowsill. The house is attached to the parish church — the priest lives beside his congregation. Simple, clean, organized.
children.notes: The Tesla family residence in Smiljan. Milutin Tesla served as parish priest here.

assets.name: Gospic_Town_1863
assets.notes: Market town in the Lika valley, 15km from Smiljan. Where the Tesla family relocated after Dane's death. The Church of the Holy Great Martyr George is in Gospic.

children.name: Church_Holy_Great_Martyr_George_1863
children.physique: Small Serbian Orthodox church in Gospic, Croatia. Stone construction with a modest bell tower. Whitewashed interior walls with Orthodox iconography. Wooden pews worn smooth from decades of use. Beeswax candle scent and old stone cool. Small windows letting in narrow shafts of light. Hymn books on the pews — paper booklets with printed Serbian text.
children.notes: Where M.K.'s grandmother saw two Tesla boys — one drawing machines on the back of the hymnal, one singing. In the alternate timeline, both Dane and Nikola attended this church.

children.name: Gospic_Historical_Museum_1981
children.physique: Small regional museum building, stone exterior, modest interior. A reading room with shelves of bound transcripts and documents. Fluorescent overhead lighting. Wooden tables. The Lika Cultural Documentation Society transcripts stored in bound volumes on numbered shelves. Unindexed, undigitized. Paper pages in ring binders.
children.notes: Where the Lika Cultural Documentation Society transcripts were transferred in 1995 after flooding destroyed the Karlovac office. Volume Seven contains the M.K. interview.

assets.name: Hotel_New_Yorker_1943
assets.notes: Art deco hotel, 43 stories, 34th and 8th Avenue, Manhattan. Tesla's home for his final decade. Where the OAP seized his 80 trunks of personal effects.

children.name: Room_3327_1943
children.physique: Corner room on 33rd floor. Two walls of curtained windows. Cramped, dark. A wood desk near the window with hotel napkins covered in equations. Single bed against the north wall. Steamer trunks and filing boxes stacked floor to ceiling. Among them: one trunk bearing a different label — D. Tesla, correspondence. Steam radiator beneath the window. The air in the room has the particular stillness of a sealed vessel. Three pigeon feathers on the windowsill.
children.notes: Room number divisible by 3, per Tesla's requirement. The D. Tesla correspondence item appears in the OAP inventory taken from this room.

assets.name: Tesla_Laboratory_Grand_Street_1891
assets.notes: Tesla's laboratory at 175 Grand Street, New York. Where the polyphase motor patents and early resonance experiments were developed. Address confirmed in historical records.

children.name: Laboratory_Interior_1891
children.physique: Large working laboratory space with high ceilings. Brick walls. Wood workbenches along two walls with electrical apparatus mounted on them — coils of copper wire, glass vacuum tubes, iron cores, brass fittings. A large blackboard on the far wall covered in equations written in two different handwriting styles. The right side of the board: angular, forward-leaning script (Tesla's). The left side: rounder, more deliberate letters. Gas lamps overhead. The smell of ozone and hot copper.
children.notes: As depicted in the laboratory photograph from the New Haven auction lot. Two men working — one at the workbench, one at the blackboard. The alternate-timeline laboratory where both Tesla brothers worked.

assets.name: Danes_Notebook_1865
assets.physique: A notebook, hand-stitched binding, no printed lines on the pages — blank paper for drawing. Approximately 20cm by 15cm. The covers are plain dark cloth, worn at the corners. Inside: dense drawings of mechanical systems that look like the interior of clockwork but are not any clock that exists. Gears interlocking at non-standard angles. Coil systems. A rotating element at the center of several designs. Some pages drawn in angular, precise lines; other pages drawn in a rounder, more patient hand. The two handwriting styles are visible even in the drawings — two different approaches to the same subject.
assets.notes: Found by Djuka Tesla while going through Dane's belongings, approximately 2 years after his death. The object that prompted the letter to her cousin in Gracac. Contains drawings in two different handwritings — the anomaly Djuka noticed but could not complete the sentence about.

assets.name: Patent_Application_Photograph_1891
assets.physique: A black-and-white photographic reproduction of a U.S. patent application cover sheet. Approximately 20cm by 28cm — standard document size. The paper shows water staining along the right margin, obscuring parts of the text. The cover sheet is headed with the U.S. Patent Office letterhead. The applicant field lists two names — the first clearly legible: N. Tesla, 175 Grand Street, New York. The second name is partially obscured by water damage: visible are the initial D and the final three letters -sla. The filing date field shows: March, 1891. The invention category field reads: Electrical Transmission — Resonant. The paper photograph shows age — yellowed at the edges, handled many times.
assets.notes: From the New Haven estate auction lot of 2003. Original application not in searchable Patent Office records. The damage to the second applicant's name is sufficient to prevent positive identification while preserving the shape of the evidence.

assets.name: Laboratory_Photograph_1891
assets.physique: A black-and-white photographic print, approximately 18cm by 24cm. Shows a laboratory interior. Two men. The first is seated at a workbench in the foreground, profile turned slightly away, one hand extended toward the second man — the gesture of passing something across. A tall man folded into a workbench chair that was built for shorter people. The second man stands at a large blackboard in the background, back to the camera, hand raised to write. The blackboard is filled with equations. The handwriting visible on the left section of the board is rounder and more deliberate than the handwriting on the right. No caption. No date. Album notation only: laboratory interior, undated.
assets.notes: From the same New Haven auction lot as the patent photograph. Described only as 'laboratory interior, undated' in the catalog. Equipment visible in the background places it in the late 1880s or early 1890s. Second man at the blackboard is never identified.

assets.name: OAP_Inventory_Document_1943
assets.physique: A multi-page typed government inventory document on official Office of Alien Property letterhead. Standard government typeface, numbered items. Item 1247 reads: D. Tesla — correspondence, three items. In the margin beside this entry: a penciled annotation in one hand reading 'clerical error — see N. Tesla.' Below it, in a different ink and a clearly different handwriting: 'Vol. XII removed for separate review — handwriting inconsistency.' The second annotation is underlined once. No further annotation follows.
assets.notes: The OAP seizure inventory from Tesla's Hotel New Yorker room, January 1943. Real historical document — the seizure is documented. The specific item and annotations are fabricated. Volume XII is never identified or described elsewhere in the inventory.

assets.name: The_Horse_1863
assets.physique: A grey stallion, large for a working animal in rural Croatia — tall at the shoulder, broad chest, long legs. His coat is a dark dapple grey, mane kept roughly trimmed. He has the habit of shifting his weight from foot to foot when confined, giving him an appearance of contained restlessness. In the garden scene: standing near the barn entrance, weight shifting, ears back, something in his attention that is not ordinary. He is looking at something that the eye cannot locate.
assets.notes: The Tesla family's horse. Previously saved Milutin Tesla's life under undescribed circumstances. Responsible (Tesla's word) for Dane Tesla's fatal injuries. The episode's primary recontextualizing symbol — introduced as instrument of accident, revealed as instrument of selection.
